[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]

== Biography ==
John Glasgow was born before 1661. He was the son of [[Glasgow-1150|James Glasgow]] and [[Duncan-16106|Agnes Duncan]].<ref>Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950. FamilySearch database. https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XTPZ-B5P (accessed 2025).</ref> He was baptized on 30 August 1661 at Edinburgh Parish, Edinburgh, Midlothian, Scotland.

Baptism locations for their children suggest that John Glasgow and his wife [[Spark-330|Agnes Spark]] moved from Kilwinning parish to Stevenston parish sometime between 1687 and 1701.

From Elaine Comes: "[[Glasgow-1055|William Glasgow (abt.1701-)]] had a brother named [[Glasgow-1056|Hugh Glasgow (abt.1692-)]] who married [[Kilpatrick-1635|Janet (Kilpatrick) Glasgow]]. They were sons of [[Glasgow-1080|John Glasgow]] and [[Spark-330|Agnes (Spark) Glasgow]]."

From baptism records, they also had a son [[Glasgow-1058|George Glasgow (bef.1687-)]], baptized in Kilwinning.<ref>Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950. FamilySearch database. https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XTVB-MX8 (accessed 2025).</ref>

== Research Notes ==
=== Kilwinning family reassessment, 22 October 2026 ===

The existing Hugh [[Glasgow-1056]] → father John [[Glasgow-1057]] relationship is now probable, 74%, superseding the earlier 58% possible assessment. The family account attributed to Elaine Comes identifies Hugh, husband of Janet Kilpatrick, as William Glasgow’s brother and names their parents John Glasgow and Agnes Spark. William’s held Stevenston child citation names that same parental couple, also recorded with George at Kilwinning in 1687. Hugh’s Kilwinning family from 1710 belongs to the same local generation. These specific people, spouse and household make John-1057 the probable father. The incorrect Glasgow-1080 hyperlink in John’s duplicate quotation is an editorial inconsistency: Hugh’s own captured account links John-1057 correctly and both texts name John and Agnes Spark. It is not evidence for a competing parent. The household records corroborate the named couple, while Hugh’s siblinghood and transfer of that fatherhood still depend on the single secondary account; duplicated quotations are not independent testimony.

74% assesses the complete Hugh-to-John/Agnes-household father identification, from 58% possible. The sibling relationship is reported, not independently proved. No Hugh childhood record or underlying evidence for Elaine’s statement was inspected. John’s own 1661 Edinburgh-child identification, the unrelated 1685 testament comparison, other ancestry and all mothers retain separate assessments. The circa-1692/1700 estimates are not birth records; no dates are changed.

Next useful evidence: Find the underlying evidence for Elaine’s specific brother/parent statement, or an identifying marriage, apprenticeship or inheritance record for Hugh. Rechecking the broken hyperlink alone cannot resolve the historical relationship.

=== Father confidence review, 22 October 2026 ===

The existing father [[Glasgow-1150]] is assessed at 97% (proved). John’s 30 August 1661 Edinburgh baptism names James Glasgow and Agnes Duncan. James-1150’s 1653 marriage to Agnes and her 1674 burial as the weaver’s wife fit the same named couple and ordered household. The combined couple evidence identifies the father more securely than the baptism name alone.

The Edinburgh child and James/Agnes household; OPR685/1,60/225, original uninspected. John’s later identification with the Ayrshire John/Agnes Spark adult is not established by this rating; the separate Duffe identity remains qualified.

Next useful test: Test the Edinburgh child to Ayrshire adult continuity, not the explicit baptism parent clause.

Source basis already held: [https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XTPZ-B5P Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950, entry for Johne Glasgow, 1661. https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XTPZ-B5P]. No new original was inspected in this review. This is an assessment of an existing attachment, not a new father.


=== Possible Irvine–Dundonald identity and ancestry ===

Prefer the Irvine father account William [[Glasgow-1055]] as the same adult as the Dundonald weaver William [[Glasgow-3586]], at 56% subjective identity confidence. The Irvine entries name Wm or William as father of Grizell in 1724, Agnes in 1725, Katherine in 1727 and Margaret in 1729. The Dundonald entry names William Glasgow, weaver at Achenyeards, as Jean’s father on 1 October 1732. An existing adult household in the adjoining Irvine parish followed by the 1732 Dundonald household is a specific chronological and local fit, and is preferred to matching an otherwise untraced childhood profile alone. This is an inferred adult identity: the Irvine transcripts do not state the father’s trade or Achenyeards residence.

Select John [[Glasgow-1057]] as the Dundonald William’s possible working father at 46%. This is an assessment of the complete father proposition, including both the 56% adult identity and the further identification of the Irvine adult with the Stevenston child cited as born or baptised on 30 November 1700 to John Glasgow and Agnas Spark (OPR615,10/3,frame11). The current William-1055 account estimates 1701; the citation and estimate are not silently harmonised. John-1057 is the existing account for that named parent. Its separate identification with an Edinburgh child baptised in1661, and its own earlier ancestry, retain their existing qualifications. The percentages are individual judgments, not measured frequencies or independent values to multiply.

No record names the Dundonald father’s own parents, connects the two adult households, or supplies an occupation for the Irvine father. William [[Glasgow-3288]], baptised at Kilbirnie on20August1704, remains a compatible alternative. William [[Glasgow-1061]], whose maintained transcript gives birth25June1715 and baptism26June1715 at Byres,Kilwinning, could have been a father at seventeen in1732; this is a weaker generation fit, not an exclusion. An unrepresented William remains possible. No wife’s death, remarriage, exact migration or craft inheritance is invented. Katherine’s1727 transcript names Mary Monfodd, while the other three Irvine entries name Margaret with Monfood/Montford/Montfod variants; this maternal distinction remains unresolved. The undated Mary Montfort marriage attached to William-1061 cannot identify the1727 mother merely by her name. No maternity is transferred from either William account.

The two William profiles remain separate accounts, with no merge and no claim of two proved William sons. Jean’s existing father link stays ungraded. The1733 child’s selected father remains possible52%, and Barbara Stevenson’s maternity remains99%; neither is strengthened by this upstream hypothesis. Jean’s mother remains unknown. Barbara’s existing pairing with the Dundonald father is ungraded and does not establish a remarriage after the Irvine household. Preserve all vital fields and previously selected relatives. Resolve the possible duplicate before a live attachment or merger. This is one new possible father proposal based on reassessment of held transcripts and profile citations; no original parish register was newly inspected and no live edit is made.

James Richmond’s Irvine account in the Old Statistical Account,volume7,printedpp169–170 (PDFpages1–2), describes the part of the settlement south of the river as belonging to Dundonald parish. The inspected printed page supports close geographical context, not this man’s residence in that part of Irvine or an individual migration in1732.

Inspect the original Irvine1724–1729 and Dundonald1732–1733 entries for the father’s occupation, residence and witnesses, and compare the Stevenston1700 entry with the adult’s later household. Seek a marriage, tenancy or kirk-session record distinguishing the Irvine father from William-3288 and William-1061. Test Mary versus Margaret independently; do not create a wife’s death to explain a later pairing.<ref name="IrvineDundonald2026">[https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FBAP%2F3573951&tab=this Grizell Glasgow, 09 Aug 1724, Irvine; held Findmypast transcript]; [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FBAP%2F3574073&tab=this Agnes Glasgow, 07 Dec 1725, Irvine; held Findmypast transcript]; [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FBAP%2F3574234&tab=this Katherine Glasgow, 03 Sep 1727, Irvine; held Findmypast transcript]; [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FBAP%2F3574367&tab=this Margaret Glasgow, 05 Jan 1729, Irvine; held Findmypast transcript]; [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FBAP%2F3536699&tab=this Jean Glasgow, 01 Oct 1732, Dundonald; held Findmypast transcript]; [https://stataccscot.ed.ac.uk/data/pdfs/account1/StAS.1.7.169.P.Ayrshire.Irvine.pdf#page=2 James Richmond, Old Statistical Account, Irvine,vol7,p170 / PDFpage2; geography only]. === Selected uncertain family — 16 October 2026 ===

Select John [[Glasgow-1057]] and Agnes [[Spark-330]] as the uncertain working parents of George [[Glasgow-4165]], father with Margt at Irvine in 1741–1745. The preferred model uses possible identity with their son George [[Glasgow-1058]], baptised at Kilwinning on 20 November 1687 and already associated with the George/Margaret Martain couple indexed marrying there on 11 June 1728. That couple’s son George-3312 is indexed at Kilwinning in 1729. The nearby Irvine household later repeats George and Margt, with no maternal surname or father’s age stated. This offers a specific existing couple and a compatible continuation across neighbouring parishes. On an infant-baptism assumption, the elder George would be about 54–58 at the Irvine children; late fatherhood remains possible. Margaret’s circa 1704 estimate would fit an adult mother in 1741–1745, but it is only a marriage-derived estimate. Neither calculation proves the identities or a move.

The 1687 child, 1728 groom and Irvine father may be different men. The match of Margt to Margaret Martin is compatible, not a full recorded maternal surname match, and no age, occupation or property bridges the two parishes. The existing 1687-child/1728-adult family account also needs its identity assessment kept separate from the child’s explicit parent clause. A younger George from the Irvine Hugh/Service, James/Rae or another local family remains possible. The proposed father James-4158 would give a normal generation if George was born around 1720, but no record names him as George’s father; the specific older George/Margaret household is preferred provisionally. Keep the merchant son George-3312 distinct. If his 1729 entry represents infant baptism, he would be only about 12 at the 1741 fatherhood, a strong objection to assigning those children directly to that son. The index event type and adult-child identities still require their own review; an unsupported older birth estimate must not decide them. No merchant trade, Nethermains ownership, Manchester patent or artillery career is transferred to the Irvine father. No identity merge, duplicate removal or live relationship save is performed.

The 1687 child’s confident parentage stays as previously marked. The Irvine adult account does not establish another distinct George son.
